---
title: "References & Recommendations"
---

## General recommendations (books)

Wilke, Claus O. 2019. *Fundamentals of Data Visualization*. O'Reilly Media. ([read online for free](https://clauswilke.com/dataviz/))

- Excellent overview with practical advice
- Software agnostic

Healy, Kieran. 2018. *Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction*. Princeton University Press. ([read online for free](https://socviz.co/))

- Helpful for applied researchers as the book covers model visualization (few others do). Focused on R and ggplot.
- I recommend the preface and Chapter 1 to everyone---even if you never plan to use R

Schwabish, Jonathan. 2021. *[Better Data Visualizations](https://cup.columbia.edu/book/better-data-visualizations/9780231193115).* Columbia University Press.

- Excellent general overview
- Software agnostic

## General recommendations (articles)

### Overview of data visualization

Franconeri, S. L., Padilla, L. M., Shah, P., Zacks, J. M., & Hullman, J. (2021). The science of visual data communication: What works. *Psychological Science in the Public Interest*, *22*(3), 110-161.

### Overview of making predictions and calculating marginal effects in R

Rohrer, J. M., & Arel-Bundock, V. (2026). Models as prediction machines: how to convert confusing coefficients into clear quantities. *Advances in Methods and Practices in Psychological Science*, *9*(2).

### Substantive articles with many visualizations

Mize, T. D., & Kincaid, R. (2025). [Role-Accumulation and Mental Health across the Life Course](/research/mize_kincaid_asr_2025.qmd). *American Sociological Review*, 00031224241313394.

Mize, T. D. (2025). [Competence perceptions at the intersection of gender and race-ethnicity](/research/mize_2025_spq.qmd). *Social Psychology Quarterly*, *88*(2), 271-284.
